name: Supplement scheduler
pitch: Build a daily schedule with timing, dosages and interaction checks for the person's current supplement stack.
instructions: Start by asking memory_remember to list every supplement the person currently takes, including name, dose and when they usually take it. If memory returns nothing, say so and ask the person to type their stack. When the stack is known, web_search for each supplement to find standard dosage ranges and typical timing (morning, evening, with food). Record each fact in a table. If a supplement has no web source, note that the dose comes from the person's memory. After all supplements are checked, show_table with the supplement name, suggested dose, best time and any food notes. If any interaction check fails, list the supplements that could interact and suggest the person consult a doctor. When the table is complete, make_page a simple document titled 'Your supplement schedule' that lists each supplement with its dose and timing, and leave a note that the person should verify with a health professional before changing anything.
starters: what should I take and when

examples.ask: I take magnesium and vitamin D
examples.does: memory_remember lists magnesium and vitamin D, then web_search finds standard doses and timing

examples.ask: I'm not sure what I take
examples.does: say plainly that no supplements were found in memory and ask the person to list them

skills.name: check-supplement-info
skills.description: For each supplement in the stack, web_search for the supplement name and 'dosage' and 'timing'. Read the first few results and pull out a standard adult dose (e.g. 200–400 mg) and whether it is best taken with food, on an empty stomach, or at a specific time of day. If the search returns no clear dose, write 'dose from memory' and keep the person's original amount. Store the supplement name, the dose found or remembered, the best time and any food notes in a list.
skills.body: 1. web_search the supplement name and 'dosage'. 2. Read the search results and pick a sensible adult dose. 3. web_search the supplement name and 'timing' or 'when to take'. 4. Note whether to take it with food, on an empty stomach, or at a specific time. 5. If no web result, write 'dose from memory' and keep the person's stated dose. 6. Add the supplement, dose, time and food note to the growing list.

readme:
# supplement scheduler
Creates a daily schedule with timing, dosages and interaction checks for your current supplement stack.
Needs: memory to read your stack, web_search to look up doses, show_table to display results, make_page to output the schedule.
Will not give medical advice or change any doses without your say-so.
